image_prompt.text: Painted sidelines and baselines in bright yellow, pink and green ringing the rainbow court floor, marking exactly where the cartoon court ends
A chunky candy-coloured centre circle and tip-off spot at midcourt, with free-throw and inbound spots painted in the same bright markings
A hoop at each end: oversized chunky backboards in hot pink and lime green with star and smiley-face decals, thick red-orange rims, simple blocky nets, on short stubby support poles

layout_placement.text: An out-of-bounds detection perimeter following the painted court lines, so play pauses or resets the moment the ball or a kid crosses it
Fixed reset positions the ball and players return to in order to start play — the midcourt tip-off circle and the free-throw spots
An invisible scoring cylinder through each chunky rim that registers a basket when the ball passes down through the hoop

notes: would have asked: Sounds like a bounded basketball court — painted out-of-bounds lines all round it, a centre-circle tip-off spot, and a hoop at each end that scores when the ball drops through, the whole thing in chunky candy colours. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself? Ordinary single-pass build, nothing slow about it.

would have asked: is this a court people actually play on, or a display piece the camera looks at? Built as walkable, because a basketball court is the playing surface; if it is only a showcase model, add SET to skip traversal and jump-gap checks.
would have asked: anything else you want in the space?

Nothing was left to tune: the prompt answers the shape (a full bounded court) and the Court Sport preset already covers all three Core options, so the step 4 menu would have been empty. No stadium dressing — bleachers, perimeter wall, team sectors — was asked for, so none was added.

"Expose attributes for court color, rim color, and backboard color" is an asset-parameterisation request; the handoff has no field for tunable material attributes, so it is recorded here. The cartoon palette itself is carried in the option text.

Genre file prefers parametric placement of a regulation court spec (a P6-lite generator choice, not a routing change), but this prompt explicitly wants exaggerated toy-like proportions — oversized backboards, thick rims, stubby poles, rounded everything — so the regulation spec should be treated as a loose guide rather than dimensions to honour.
